newsitem.title: CHINA: Five foreign banks for Shanghai branch approval.
newsitem.headline: Five foreign banks for Shanghai branch approval.

text.p: Five more foreign banks have received approval or are close to gaining approval to open full branches in Shanghai, foreign bankers said on Thursday.

Three of the banks have already received approval -- South Korea's Hanil Bank, Japan's Tokai Bank and Belgium's Kredietbank, while two others -- France's Banque Paribas and Chase Manhattan -- are close to receiving the final word, they said.

The five will take the total number of foreign banks and institutions with full branch rights in Shanghai to 46. This includes one Sino-French joint venture bank, four insurance firms and three finance companies.
A spokeswoman for the PBOC declined to comment on the status of the pending applications, saying it was impossible to talk about them before they received final approval.
A foreign banker said it was expected that the banks with new full branches would be able to start business by March or April next year.
He said it was crucial for a foreign bank to gain full branch status in Shanghai. "This is the fastest growing market for foreign banks in China, so it is very important to be a player here."
